official.deadline_note: CBS publishes 15 January 23:59 CET as the admission and scholarship deadline for non-EU/EEA applicants who need a student residence permit (application group 2). A separate Winter application round, open only to the MSc in Business Administration and Digital Business, closes 15 October 2026 for study start 1 February 2027, and CBS states this is the last winter intake for that programme.
official.application_cycle: September intake, application group 2 (non-EU/EEA applicants needing a student residence permit); application portal opens 15 December
official.status_note: CBS states it receives a limited number of government scholarships each year to fund highly qualified full-degree students from non-EU/EEA countries. Applicants offered a scholarship are notified by 15 March at the latest via the Application Portal; applicants who are accepted but not offered a scholarship receive an invoice for the first tuition fee payment.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "Each scholarship includes a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend of DKK 8,000 to assist with living costs in Denmark. The grant has a maximum duration of 22 months, starting 1 September the year you are accepted (1 February if you are accepted in the Winter application round)."
official.funding_period: per month, for a maximum of 22 months

official.application_route: One application per programme in the Danish Application Portal: apply for admission, tick the option to be considered for the CBS scholarship, and upload a maximum 2-page personal statement by 15 January 23:59 CET.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/non-EEA/non-Swiss citizens who need a student residence permit to live and study in Denmark.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is for highly qualified full-degree students from countries outside the EU/EEA who need a student residence permit.

applicant_utility.summary: Roughly 25 CBS scholarships a year are shared across every graduate programme, so your real competition is that pool of 25 rather than your own programme, and the decision rests on academic record, English proficiency and a maximum two-page personal statement rather than financial need. You have to actively tick the scholarship box in the Danish Application Portal and upload that statement by 15 January 23:59 CET, and the older winter route through the MSc in Business Administration and Digital Business closed its last intake on 15 October 2026. Winners hear by 15 March, and the DKK 8,000 arrives monthly in advance, so budget enough savings to cover your first Copenhagen months before the first banking day of September.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants with a strong, well-documented bachelor record heading for a CBS master's who can pay the application fee and write a sharp, programme-specific personal statement.
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the application fee before the deadline or upload exemption documentation, since a missing fee makes you ineligible for the scholarship
Book IELTS/TOEFL at least three to four weeks early so CBS can verify the result with the provider by the deadline
Prepare a bachelor transcript that is signed and stamped or carries an online verification code, showing ECTS for every course
Draft the personal statement to exactly two pages or less and tie it explicitly to the CBS programme you applied for
Check the individual programme's admission page for its ECTS and language thresholds before committing to a priority
Register early in the portal and add no-reply@umit.dk to your safe senders so you never miss a deadline message
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the scholarship can be added after the 15 January deadline - it cannot
Applying for admission without ticking the scholarship box, so the file is never assessed for funding
A language test result CBS cannot verify with the provider by the deadline, because no documentation can be added afterwards
Being eligible for SU or another form of Danish public support, which disqualifies you outright
Falling more than 30 ECTS behind the study plan, switching programme, or letting the student residence permit lapse, which ends the grant
Leaving the application fee unpaid when you do not hold a Danish bachelor degree
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The application fee, the two residence-permit application fees CBS lists for non-EEA/EU students applying from abroad, flights to Denmark, a housing deposit and insurance. CBS does not publish what DKK 8,000 per month leaves uncovered in Copenhagen, so assume the gap between the stipend and real living costs is funded by you.
document_audit: The personal statement is capped at two pages - longer submissions work against you, not for you
Transcripts must be colour scans with the university logo, stamp and signature, or digitally signed with a verification code
Course descriptions must be official university documents; ones you write yourself are not accepted
Dual citizens must upload both passports, and anyone with permanent residence elsewhere must upload that permit too
Nothing can be uploaded after the deadline, so the file has to be complete on 15 January
alerts: The award is merit-based, not need-based, so a strong motivation and academic story matters more than documenting hardship
About 25 awards for all graduate programmes makes the odds slim, so apply to other Danish and European funding in parallel
The 22-month cap matches the standard two years; extensions are granted only in extraordinary circumstances such as severe illness
The 22-month clock starts on the acceptance date, and the last winter-round entry point (15 October 2026, study start 1 February 2027) is a single-programme route that CBS is discontinuing
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Submit one application per programme (up to three) in the Danish Application Portal by 15 January, tick the scholarship option, upload the personal statement, then wait for the portal answer by 15 March.

official.deadline_note: There is no separate scholarship deadline: AAU's September-intake application deadline for fee-paying applicants (non-EU/EEA) is 15 January 23:59 CET, while non-fee-paying applicants (primarily EU/EEA) have until 1 March 23:59 CET. Scholarship decisions are communicated by the beginning of July at the latest, though they may come earlier.
official.application_cycle: September intake only; scholarships are granted per September intake only and the Application Portal opens medio December
official.status_note: AAU grants approximately 15 scholarships each September intake and states it will inform all applicants about the scholarship decision by the beginning of July at the latest, though it may be earlier.
official.tuition_coverage_note: "A scholarship consists of a tuition fee waiver and a monthly stipend aimed at covering living expenses during the four semesters of your master's programme."

Academic qualifications, which AAU states transcend national borders and are essentially global
coverage: Tuition fee waiver for the master's programme
Monthly living-expense stipend aimed at covering living expenses during the four semesters
application_method: All non-EU applicants are automatically considered when applying to a master's programme
Apply through the AAU Application Portal and upload the application fee receipt to each application
official.application_route: Apply to a fee-paying master's programme in the AAU Application Portal by 15 January 23:59 CET; scholarship consideration is automatic, with no separate form.
official.citizenship_residency: Non-EU/EEA citizens who pay tuition and do not hold one of the Danish residence permits listed by AAU that exempt students from application and tuition fees.
official.international_eligibility: Yes - the scholarship is exclusively for applicants from outside the EU/EEA; AAU states EU/EEA students cannot apply for scholarships at AAU.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Applies to fee-paying master's programmes for the September intake only.
official.duration: Four semesters, the standard duration of a master's degree; no stipend is paid beyond the first two years of study if the programme is prolonged.
official.description: The scholarships are financed by the Danish Government and awarded by Aalborg University: each September intake AAU grants a limited number, approximately 15, to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications.
official.program_type: Danish government-financed tuition fee waiver plus monthly living stipend, awarded by the university
official.english_requirement: IELTS Academic 6.5 overall band score with a minimum of 6.0 in each section, or TOEFL iBT 85 with a minimum of 20 in each section (Cambridge C2 Proficiency at C1, C1 Advanced grade C and ECPE passed are also accepted). Tests must be less than 2 years old by the application deadline, and AAU does not accept IELTS One Skill Retake, TOEFL Essentials or MyBest scores, Duolingo or PTE.

applicant_utility.summary: There is no scholarship form to fill in: every non-EU/EEA applicant to a fee-paying AAU master's is considered automatically once the programme application is submitted, so the only thing you control is filing it, with the application-fee receipt attached, before the 15 January fee-paying deadline. Only about 15 awards exist per September intake and AAU openly warns the DKK 11,225 monthly stipend may not cover all living expenses in Denmark. Decisions arrive by the beginning of July, long after the 10 April admission answer, so you must be able to carry the first semester tuition while you wait or rely on the refund AAU promises if the scholarship is granted after you have paid.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Non-EU/EEA applicants to higher-tuition AAU technical and engineering master's, where the fee waiver is worth most, who can document a strong bachelor record and self-fund the first months.
application_readiness_checklist: Pay the 150 EUR / 1,150 DKK application fee through the AAU webshop and upload the receipt to each of your applications
Hold yourself to three priorities in the portal, because more than three is rejected without further notice
Merge every multi-page document into a single PDF under the 10 MB limit before uploading
Book an approved English test early; a registration receipt is enough at application, but the final result for non-EU applicants without a Danish permit is due 20 April for the September intake
Get stamped, signed and translated transcripts and diploma ready before the portal opens in mid-December
common_rejection_risks: Missing the 15 January fee-paying deadline, which is months earlier than the EU/EEA 1 March deadline and is not extended
Listing more than three programme priorities, which AAU rejects without further notice
Sending documents by post or email, or uploading unmerged or oversized PDFs
Using a provisional certificate for a degree completed more than a year ago
Relying on the stipend as your full living budget, since AAU states the scholarship might not cover all living expenses
Counting on the available-study-places route later, since non-EU citizens cannot use it unless they hold an exempting residence permit
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The non-refundable application fee, residence-permit costs, flights, accommodation deposit, insurance and any living costs above the DKK 11,225 monthly stipend, which AAU says may need to be supplemented from savings, a home-country loan or a student job.

Documents must be signed and stamped by the issuing university and translated into English, Danish, Swedish or Norwegian
Upload the fee receipt to every application, not only the first one
English tests must be under two years old at the deadline, and all section minimums must be met in a single sitting
If you hold a Danish residence permit, add both the permit card and the letter
alerts: The scholarship decision can land after the tuition payment deadline, so plan your cash flow and claim the refund if you have already paid
Stipend payments can be retroactive if your CPR number, NemKonto and tax registration are not in place by 1 September
Only September-intake applicants are considered; February intake applications are not part of the scholarship round
AAU explicitly advises not to rely solely on receiving a scholarship when applying
Non-EU/EEA students taking supplementary courses pay an additional fee per ECTS, ranging from DKK 287 to DKK 760 depending on the programme
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply in the AAU portal (dans.stads.dk) by 15 January 23:59 CET with the fee receipt attached; the admission answer follows on 10 April and the scholarship answer by the beginning of July.
